blindSummary:
In 2024 a trans woman was the victim of an attempted femicide in this state/province's principal city. The court imposed four years of part-time detention against the five years of full-time detention the prosecution had sought; the victim's mother publicly denounced the downgrading of an attack motivated by her daughter's gender identity. In April 2026 the regional director of the national women-and-gender-equality service publicly criticised the sentence as failing to reflect the gravity of the attack and announced an appeal - a named institutional pushback that partly offsets the judicial under-penalisation. The state/province also ranked among those with the largest percentage increases in the 2024 dataset and holds 0.96 % of the national case total.

Local risk sits slightly below the country-wide level. The under-sentencing for gender-motivated violence against a trans woman is a concrete traveler-relevant severity finding; the service's appeal is a genuine institutional counter-signal that prevents a deeper deduction. Set against another state/province whose court annulment voids femicide protection for trans women outright in that jurisdiction, this one scores slightly higher: there the protection is annulled entirely, whereas here the femicide framework was applied but under-sentenced, and the national service is actively appealing to correct the record.

For a visitor, practical exposure here is low absolute case volume (0.96 % of the national total), but the judicial precedent of reduced sentences for attacks on trans women is a severity signal placing the state/province just below the country-wide level.
